decisive_items: a destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the right maxillary sinus, forming a large soft-tissue mass
within the cystic portion, a fluid-fluid level was identified
serial imaging over two weeks showed rapid enlargement of the mass
response.rationale: Rapidly enlarging destructive maxillary sinus/orbital mass with fluid-fluid level and heterogeneous enhancement in a toddler is classic for rhabdomyosarcoma; cellulitis is excluded by bone destruction and antibiotic failure, while LCH and Ewing sarcoma are less consistent with this imaging tempo and pattern.

rejected.why: Langerhans cell histiocytosis can cause destructive sinus/orbital lesions, but the rapid enlargement, fluid-fluid level, and heterogeneously enhancing soft-tissue mass favor a sarcoma.
Orbital cellulitis explains the initial erythema and swelling but cannot account for the destructive bone lesion, soft-tissue mass, and persistence despite antibiotics.
Ewing sarcoma is a malignant small round cell tumor, but rhabdomyosarcoma is far more common in this age group and head-neck location with this imaging pattern.
